transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been having this issue when people are talking to me. 

Like, people at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them, but then... I just realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. I always end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It happens enough that I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
Does this difficulty with staying focused during conversations happen in other areas of your life as well, such as when you are trying to complete a task or listen to instructions at work?

Yeah, it does happen with other things too. I'm not working anymore, so I don't have work instructions to worry about, but... well, if I sit down with a gallery packet or a set of notes for the museum, I'll usually start out fine. 

But after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes are still just moving over the page, while my mind has completely wandered off somewhere else. I always end up having to go back and read the exact same part over again just to actually take in what it says.
Do you often feel like you have a motor running inside you, or do you find it difficult to sit still for long periods of time?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel like I have a motor running or anything. I don't really have any trouble sitting still, either. I can sit in a chair for a good long while without feeling like I need to get up and move around. It's more just my mind that wanders off, not my body.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling worried or anxious about various aspects of your life?

No, not really. I don't spend much time worrying about things. I mean, I have the usual concerns anyone my age might have, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious or worried on a regular basis. It's really just the focus thing that's been bothering me.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, do you remember having these same difficulties with focus and attention back then?

Yeah, I do. Even back in grade school, actually. I remember my report cards always said things like "daydreams a lot" or "needs reminders to finish his work." And my mother... well, she used to have to sit right next to me while I did my homework just to keep me on track. That was before I was twelve, I think. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
